title: European quality systems
subtitle: AOC, DOCG, DO and Prädikat
objectives: Name the national terms for PDO and PGI
Explain the extra tiers in Italy and Spain

steps.title: National names
steps.body: Each EU country names its levels. France: AOC or AOP for PDO, IGP or Vin de Pays for PGI. Italy: DOCG and DOC for PDO, IGT for PGI. Spain: DOCa or DOQ and DO for PDO, Vino de la Tierra for PGI. Portugal: DOC for PDO, Vinho Regional for PGI.
steps.highlight: AOC, DOC, DO: the PDO family

steps.title: Extra steps
steps.body: Italy's DOCG is a top tier, with stricter rules and tasting approval; Barolo and Chianti Classico are DOCG. Spain's DOCa, for Rioja and Priorat, works similarly. Germany's PDO wines are graded partly by sugar in the grapes at harvest: Qualitätswein, then Prädikatswein with six levels, from Kabinett to Trockenbeerenauslese.
steps.highlight: DOCG and DOCa sit above DOC and DO

steps.prompt: Match each term to its country.
steps.explanation: Every EU country uses its own words for the same two levels, sometimes with extra tiers.

steps.body: When a label from Europe names a region and nothing else, it's usually a PDO. Look up the rules once and you'll know the grape for life: Chablis is Chardonnay, Sancerre is Sauvignon Blanc, Barolo is Nebbiolo.

steps.prompt: Order Germany's Prädikat levels from least to most ripe.
steps.explanation: Eiswein sits beside Beerenauslese in required ripeness, but is made from frozen grapes.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Each EU country has its own names for PDO and PGI
Italy's DOCG and Spain's DOCa are top tiers
Germany grades Prädikatswein by ripeness at harvest
